entities.definition: Fundamental mechanisms for indirect object access in C++: pointers hold rebindable memory addresses and can be null; references are non-null immutable aliases.
keyClaims: Pointers hold addresses, can be null, and can be reassigned to different objects
References are immutable aliases that must be initialized upon creation and cannot be null
Both provide indirect access without copying values

entities.definition: Resource Acquisition Is Initialization (RAII) ties resource management directly to object lifetime so destructors automatically release resources upon leaving scope.
keyClaims: Acquires resources in constructor and releases them deterministically in destructor
Guarantees leak-free exception safety without explicit cleanup code

entities.definition: Value management semantics in C++: copying duplicates resource state whereas moving transfers ownership from rvalue objects without deep allocation.
keyClaims: Copy semantics perform deep duplication of resources
Move semantics transfer ownership of pointers and buffer handles from expiring objects
Significantly optimizes performance by eliminating redundant heap allocations

entities.definition: Language features enabling move semantics: rvalue references (T&&) bind to temporaries, and std::move is an unconditional cast to an rvalue reference.
keyClaims: Rvalue references (T&&) bind to temporary expiring values
std::move is an unconditional static_cast to rvalue reference and emits no runtime machine code by itself
std::move enables move constructors and move assignment operators during overload resolution

entities.definition: RAII wrapper classes managing heap memory lifetimes: std::unique_ptr for exclusive ownership, std::shared_ptr for reference-counted ownership, and std::weak_ptr for breaking cycles.
keyClaims: std::unique_ptr provides exclusive zero-overhead ownership and prevents copying
std::shared_ptr maintains atomic reference counting for shared ownership
std::weak_ptr prevents reference count cycles in shared pointer graphs

entities.definition: Compile-time programming paradigm in C++ using templates, SFINAE, type traits, and concepts to compute types and values at compile time.
keyClaims: Executes computation and code generation during compilation
Uses type traits and SFINAE/Concepts for compile-time type constraints and introspection
Produces zero runtime overhead for static abstractions
